slides.title: Water + sewer + stormwater: combined vs separate, Burnham, green infrastructure, SUDS + LID
slides.body:
**Urban infrastructure** — the engineered systems that keep cities functioning — divides into water + wastewater + stormwater, energy + heating + cooling, waste, communications + digital. Planning + engineering interact at every layer; infrastructure choices shape urban form for centuries.

**Water supply**:
- Sources: surface water (rivers, lakes, reservoirs — NYC Catskill + Delaware system, LA's California Aqueduct + Owens Valley, London's Thames Water); groundwater (Mexico City, much of the U.S. Plains); desalination (Singapore, San Diego, Tel Aviv); recycled / non-potable (Singapore NEWater, Orange County GWRS).
- Treatment: coagulation + filtration + disinfection (chlorine, UV, ozone). Standards: WHO + US EPA Safe Drinking Water Act 1974.
- Distribution: pumped to elevated tanks → gravity to consumers; pressure 40-100 psi typical.
- *Aging U.S. infrastructure*: ASCE report card rates U.S. water infrastructure C-/D+; ~240k water-main breaks/year; ~2.1 trillion gallons lost to leaks (~17% of treated water). Lead service lines: ~9.2M (EPA 2023 estimate); replacement is a 2021 IIJA + Lead+Copper Rule priority.

**Sanitary sewer (wastewater)**:
- Conveys sewage to wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs).
- Treatment levels: primary (screening + settling), secondary (biological — activated sludge or trickling filter), tertiary (nutrient removal, disinfection). Most U.S. WWTPs are secondary; tertiary required in nutrient-sensitive watersheds (Chesapeake Bay, Long Island Sound).
- ~14k publicly-owned WWTPs (POTWs) in the U.S.; serve ~76% of households (the rest have septic).

**Stormwater**:
- Conveys rain runoff. Two architectures:
  - **Combined sewer system (CSS)**: stormwater + sanitary sewage in one pipe. Older U.S. + European cities. ~700 U.S. communities (NYC + Philadelphia + Chicago + Boston + Pittsburgh + DC's old sections). Overflows during heavy rain — *combined sewer overflows (CSOs)* — discharge untreated sewage to rivers + harbors.
  - **Separate sewer system (SSS)**: parallel networks. Newer development. Cleaner in storms but more pipe + harder to retrofit.
- **CSO mitigation**: deep tunnels (Chicago TARP / Deep Tunnel, Indianapolis DigIndy, NYC East Side Coastal Resiliency); storage tanks; green infrastructure (next).

**Daniel Burnham + Chicago drainage**:
- **Daniel Burnham + Edward Bennett's *Plan of Chicago* (1909)** — the City Beautiful classic — included an integrated drainage + lakefront plan.
- *Chicago Sanitary + Ship Canal* (completed 1900) reversed the Chicago River's flow to drain sewage *away* from Lake Michigan (the city's water source) toward the Mississippi watershed — among the most consequential 19th-c. infrastructure projects.
- TARP / Deep Tunnel (1975-, ~109 miles + 17.5B gallon storage) is the modern continuation.

**Green infrastructure (GI) + SUDS + LID**:
- **Green Infrastructure (GI)**: rain gardens, bioswales, permeable pavement, green roofs, urban tree canopy, constructed wetlands — natural + engineered systems that capture + filter + infiltrate stormwater at the source.
- **Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SUDS)** — UK terminology + framework; **Low Impact Development (LID)** — U.S. terminology, similar concept.
- *Source control* vs *end-of-pipe* treatment: GI reduces flow + pollution where it falls, easing downstream sewer + WWTP loads.
- *Co-benefits*: heat-island reduction, biodiversity, urban-tree carbon, recreational + aesthetic value, property-value uplift.
- *Examples*: Philadelphia *Green City Clean Waters* (2011, 25-year, ~\$2.4B GI program); Portland OR *Green Streets* (curb-extension bioswales); NYC Greenways + Bioswales + Bluebelts; Copenhagen Cloudburst Management Plan post-2011 flood (~\$1.3B GI + grey hybrid); Singapore *ABC Waters* (Active, Beautiful, Clean); Berlin sponge-city (Schwammstadt).
- *Co-design with urban form*: GI integrates with the Complete Streets + 15-min city + Vision Zero agenda (lesson 3) + with environmental-justice neighborhood-greening (lesson 7).

**Performance metrics + standards**: USEPA NPDES (National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System); MS4 permits for municipal stormwater; LEED-ND + SITES credit for stormwater management.

slides.title: Energy + waste: district heating, microgrids, solar zoning, Curitiba recycling, 3-stream, circular economy
slides.body:
**Energy + heating + cooling** in cities accounts for ~60-70% of urban energy demand + a comparable share of greenhouse-gas emissions (buildings + on-site combustion + electricity + heat). Decarbonization of cities is largely about reshaping energy systems.

**District heating + cooling**:
- Centralized plant or network distributes hot water / steam (heating) or chilled water (cooling) to many buildings through insulated pipes.
- *Origins*: Lockport NY (1877, Birdsill Holly). Modern systems: Copenhagen (~98% district heating, mostly from waste-incineration + CHP + heat pumps), Helsinki (~93%), Stockholm, Hamburg, Vienna, Moscow, Beijing, NYC steam (Con Edison, the world's oldest large district-steam system).
- *Efficiency*: combined-heat-and-power (CHP / cogen) achieves ~80-90% fuel utilization vs ~33% for stand-alone electricity generation.
- *Decarbonization path*: shift from fossil-fired CHP to large heat pumps (sea + lake + sewer water as heat source — Stockholm Värtan; Drammen Norway), waste-heat recovery (data centers, industry), biomass + biogas, geothermal (Reykjavik).
- *U.S. lag*: outside major downtowns (NYC, Boston, Chicago, Detroit) + universities + military bases, district systems uncommon. Decarbonization-driven revival emerging.

**Microgrids**:
- Self-sufficient local power systems with on-site generation (solar PV, wind, batteries, CHP, fuel cells) that can island from the main grid during outages.
- Use cases: critical-facility resilience (hospitals, fire stations, water-treatment); university + military campuses; remote + island communities (Hawaii, Alaska, Caribbean post-hurricane); community microgrids (Brooklyn Microgrid, Boulder).
- *Resilience driver*: NYC post-Sandy 2012 + Puerto Rico post-María 2017 + California PSPS (Public Safety Power Shutoffs) due to wildfire risk.
- *Equity dimension*: who is on the microgrid + who is off; community-microgrid governance.

**Solar + renewable zoning**:
- *Solar rights / solar access*: laws preventing neighbors from blocking solar access (California Solar Rights Act 1978; many state + local rules).
- *Solar-ready + solar-required construction*: California 2020 mandate for new homes to include solar PV.
- *Solar zoning*: utility-scale solar siting (rural + agricultural land conflicts), urban rooftop + parking-lot canopy, agrivoltaics.
- *Building codes*: ASHRAE 90.1 + IECC + Title 24 (California) drive efficiency + electrification.
- *Heat pumps + electrification*: replacing gas furnaces + water heaters; NYC + Berkeley + Seattle + Massachusetts increasingly restricting new-construction gas connections (some preempted by state law).

**Waste management**:
- Generation: U.S. ~4.9 lb/person/day municipal solid waste (MSW); EU ~1.3 kg/day; developing-world variable.
- Hierarchy (EU + U.S. EPA): prevention > reuse > recycling > recovery (composting + energy) > disposal (landfill, incineration).
- *3-stream collection* (recyclables / organics / trash): standard in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Sweden, South Korea, Taiwan, much of Canada; U.S. adoption uneven (San Francisco mandatory composting 2009; Seattle, Portland; NYC organics collection 2023-).
- **Curitiba recycling (Brazil, 1989-)**: 'Garbage that is not garbage' — pioneering recycling + waste-pickup program; favela-resident food-for-recyclables exchange (*Câmbio Verde*); ~70% recycling rate. Pioneer of integrated waste + transit + social-policy urbanism.
- **Waste-to-energy (WtE)** + incineration: Copenhagen Amager Bakke (CopenHill, with ski slope + climbing wall on the roof) + Stockholm + Vienna Spittelau (Hundertwasser-designed) + Tokyo. Reduces landfill volume; concerns about emissions + waste-of-recyclable-material.
- **Circular economy**: Ellen MacArthur Foundation (2010-); Amsterdam Circular Strategy 2020 (first major city); Glasgow, Brussels. Reduce + reuse + remanufacture + repair + share; minimize material throughput.

**Telecommunications + utilities** (transition to next slide):
- Fiber + 5G + Wi-Fi.
- Underground utility coordination (NYC Subway + Con Ed + Verizon + city water + sewer — coordinating cuts + repairs is among the harder governance problems).

slides.title: Digital + smart city: Sidewalk Toronto, Songdo, Barcelona superblocks, digital twins, Zuboff
slides.body:
**Smart city** is the umbrella for using sensors + data + computation to manage urban systems — traffic, energy, water, waste, public safety, services. The term emerged ~2008 (IBM Smarter Planet) + has cycled through hype + critique.

**Sidewalk Labs / Sidewalk Toronto (Quayside, 2017-2020)**:
- Sidewalk Labs (Alphabet / Google subsidiary, founded 2015, led by Dan Doctoroff). Quayside on Toronto's waterfront — a 12-acre proposed development meant to demonstrate next-generation urban tech: ubiquitous sensors, autonomous vehicles, adaptive curbs, modular buildings, mass-timber construction, integrated data platform.
- *Promised features*: dynamic pricing of curb space; pedestrian-priority streets; sensor-based comfort + safety adjustments; *Urban Data Trust* to govern data.
- *Critique + collapse*: Civil-liberties + privacy concerns (Bianca Wylie + Jim Balsillie + #BlockSidewalk movement). Who owns the data; who consents; how does the *smart* infrastructure interact with democratic accountability. Toronto + Waterfront Toronto board pushed back; Sidewalk withdrew in May 2020 (citing COVID economic uncertainty + governance friction).
- *Lesson*: smart-city ambition collides with governance + privacy + democratic legitimacy when corporate ownership of urban data is the model.

**Songdo (Incheon, South Korea, 2003-)**:
- New city built from reclaimed land near Incheon Airport; ~6 km²; ~70k residents (vs ~250k planned).
- *Smart-city features*: pneumatic waste-collection tubes, sensor-equipped buildings, fiber + ubiquitous Wi-Fi, integrated LEED-certified district.
- *Outcomes*: technically impressive infrastructure; weak street life + commercial vibrancy; lower-than-projected population. The *built-from-scratch tech-utopia* model has not produced the urban vitality of organic cities.
- *Lesson*: Jacobsian fine-grain street life is hard to engineer top-down; infrastructure ≠ urbanism.

**Barcelona superblocks (Superilles, 2016-)**:
- *Ada Colau* administration (2015-23) + transport commissioner Salvador Rueda → *superblock* concept: 3×3 grid of city blocks (~400 m × 400 m) with through-traffic restricted to perimeter; interior streets pedestrian + bike + slow-traffic-priority + green-space + plazas.
- ~6 superblocks implemented; major Eixample (Cerdà) corridor *eixos verds* (green axes) underway 2020s.
- *Outcomes*: increased pedestrian + cycling traffic, reduced auto traffic + air pollution + noise in superblock interiors; some displacement of traffic to perimeter; political controversy.
- *Smart-city dimension*: sensor-based monitoring of air quality + noise + traffic; data feedback to design. But the project is fundamentally low-tech — paint + planters + bollards + community engagement, then physical redesign.
- *Lesson*: tactical urbanism + iterative redesign + community engagement can outperform high-tech utopia.

**Digital twins**:
- High-fidelity 3D + sensor-fed digital models of cities. Singapore's *Virtual Singapore* (2014-, ~\$73M Govt project); Helsinki *Helsinki 3D+*; Rennes Virtual Rennes; Boston Planning + Development Agency's 3D BIM-integrated model; Zurich's digital twin.
- Use cases: planning + design simulation; emergency management; energy + thermal-comfort modeling; visualization for participation (lesson 8).
- Tooling: ESRI ArcGIS / CityEngine; Autodesk InfraWorks; Bentley OpenCities; CityGML (open standard).
- *Caveats*: data quality + model validity; privacy (sensor + mobility data); cost; *digital twin theater* vs operational use.

**Sensors + IoT**:
- *Air quality* (PM2.5, NO₂, O₃): Breathe London, PurpleAir, Plume Labs, government networks.
- *Traffic + occupancy*: cameras, inductive loops, Bluetooth + Wi-Fi anonymous-MAC sniffing, lidar.
- *Energy + water*: smart meters; AMI (Advanced Metering Infrastructure).
- *Public safety*: ShotSpotter (controversial), gunshot detection, license-plate readers (controversial — civil-liberties).
- *Mobility*: bike-share + e-scooter telemetry; transit AVL (automatic vehicle location); MTA real-time arrival.

**Shoshana Zuboff — *The Age of Surveillance Capitalism* (2019)**:
- Harvard Business School emerita; *Surveillance capitalism* — economic logic of extracting + monetizing behavioral data, especially from urban + digital environments.
- *Critique of smart-city orthodoxy*: who owns the data, who profits, who decides; sensor-rich cities are also surveillance-rich cities.
- *Influence on regulation*: EU GDPR (2018) + AI Act (2024); California CCPA (2018); city-level data-governance frameworks (NYC Algorithm Management + Policy; Barcelona Decidim; Amsterdam Tada).
- *Lesson*: smart-city design must front-load privacy + governance + democratic accountability — not bolt them on. Sidewalk Toronto's collapse illustrated the cost of ignoring this.

**Synthesis**:
- Smart-city tech is real + useful, but governance + privacy + democratic legitimacy are first-order.
- *Tactical urbanism + community engagement* (Barcelona superblocks, NYC plazas) often outperforms big tech-utopia builds (Songdo, Sidewalk).
- The contemporary frontier (lesson 8): computational urban science (Batty, Bettencourt), AI-augmented planning, participatory tools (GIS, CityGML, Decidim), digital twins + simulation, climate-adaptation modeling.

Infrastructure is not just engineering — it is the *physical substrate* of equity (who gets reliable water + power + transit; lesson 7), climate (combined-sewer overflows during heavy rain in a hotter climate; sea-level rise threats to coastal water + waste systems), and democratic governance (data + sensors as instruments of public + private power).

question.question: Design a stormwater + CSO reduction strategy for a legacy U.S. CSS city
question.goal: A Northeast U.S. city has a combined sewer system + ~50 CSO events/year. Devise a strategy combining grey + green infrastructure + planning levers.

steps.prompt: Why does the existing CSS produce CSOs?

acceptedAnswers: stormwater + sewage share one pipe; in heavy rain the combined flow exceeds the treatment plant's hydraulic capacity + the excess (mixed stormwater + raw sewage) is released through overflow points to receiving waters

steps.reveal: In a CSS, stormwater + sanitary sewage share one pipe. Sanitary flow is roughly constant + small; stormwater flow is highly variable + can be ~100x sanitary in heavy rain. When combined flow exceeds the wastewater-treatment plant's hydraulic capacity, the pipe network is designed to relieve via *combined sewer overflow* points, dumping mixed stormwater + raw sewage to rivers / harbors. ~700 U.S. communities + ~40 million people face CSOs.

steps.prompt: What grey-infrastructure options exist + their tradeoffs?

acceptedAnswers: deep storage tunnels (chicago tarp, indianapolis digindy), surface or underground storage tanks, sewer separation (build a parallel storm-only network), and treatment-plant capacity expansion — all expensive (~$1-10B per major city) but proven and fast-acting

steps.reveal: Grey options: (1) deep storage tunnels (Chicago TARP/Deep Tunnel: 17.5B gal, ~\$4B+; Indianapolis DigIndy ~\$2B); (2) surface or underground storage tanks; (3) sewer separation — parallel storm-only network (very expensive + disruptive); (4) treatment-plant expansion. All grey: capital-intensive (\$1-10B/major city), long lead time, narrow co-benefits, but reliable + measurable performance.

steps.prompt: What green-infrastructure + planning levers complement grey?

acceptedAnswers: rain gardens + bioswales + permeable pavement + green roofs + urban tree canopy + constructed wetlands at the source; reduce impervious-surface coverage via parking-minimum elimination and complete-streets retrofit; integrate with neighborhood greening for equity + heat-island co-benefits — philadelphia gccw and portland are u.s. models

steps.reveal: GI / SUDS / LID: rain gardens, bioswales (vegetated infiltration channels), permeable pavement, green roofs, urban tree canopy, constructed wetlands — capture + infiltrate stormwater *at the source*. Planning levers: reduce impervious surface (parking-minimum elimination, lesson 2 Shoup; smaller setbacks; alleyways; tree-canopy mandates). Models: Philadelphia *Green City Clean Waters* (~\$2.4B 25-yr program), Portland Green Streets, NYC Bluebelts. Co-benefits: heat-island reduction, biodiversity, property-value uplift, equity (lesson 7) — green-infrastructure investment in underserved neighborhoods doubles as environmental-justice + public-health intervention.

steps.prompt: What does an integrated plan look like + how is success measured?

acceptedAnswers: tiered: source-control GI for small to medium storms; grey storage for large storms; treatment expansion for routine flows; embed in zoning (impervious-cap, gi requirements), capital plan, and equity scoring; measure by CSO event count + volume, water-quality data, GI acreage installed, neighborhood air-temperature + air-quality co-benefits

steps.reveal: Integrated plan: tier interventions to the storm distribution — GI handles frequent small + medium storms (the bulk of annual rainfall); grey storage tunnels + tanks handle the few large events that swamp GI; treatment-plant expansion for routine + future flows. Embed in zoning (impervious-cap, GI requirements for new development); capital + operating budget alignment; equity scoring (prioritize underserved neighborhoods). Metrics: CSO event count + volume; receiving-water quality (E. coli, DO, nutrients); GI acreage installed; co-benefits (canopy, surface-temp reduction, residents within 5-min walk of green space).

question.question: Why did the Sidewalk Toronto / Quayside project collapse, and what lesson does it offer for smart-city projects?
options: Sidewalk Labs (Alphabet/Google subsidiary, founded 2015) proposed Quayside on Toronto's waterfront (2017-2020) — a 12-acre development demonstrating sensors, autonomous vehicles, adaptive curbs, modular buildings, mass-timber construction, and an integrated data platform. The project collapsed in May 2020 after sustained civil-liberties + privacy + governance critique: Bianca Wylie + Jim Balsillie + #BlockSidewalk argued that a corporate data-owner controlling the sensor infrastructure of public space conflicted with democratic accountability + privacy + data sovereignty. Shoshana Zuboff's *Age of Surveillance Capitalism* (2019) framed the broader critique. Lesson: smart-city design must front-load privacy + data governance + democratic legitimacy. Tactical urbanism + community engagement (Barcelona superblocks) often outperform big tech-utopia builds. Infrastructure is not just engineering — it is the substrate of governance + equity + privacy.

question.question: Integrating infrastructure with planning
question.prompt: A coastal city updating its 30-year capital plan faces: aging combined sewer (~30 CSO events/year), gas-heated building stock (60% of emissions), 4 km of waterfront vulnerable to 2050 sea-level rise, and a smart-city consultant pitching sensor-everything. Propose an integrated infrastructure + planning agenda combining green stormwater infrastructure, district heating + heat-pump electrification, coastal adaptation (managed retreat + green-grey hybrid), and a Barcelona-style human-scale smart-city strategy (vs Sidewalk Toronto).

question.question: A combined sewer treatment plant has hydraulic capacity 200 MGD (million gallons/day). Dry-weather sanitary flow is 80 MGD. A storm produces 350 MGD combined flow. What CSO volume (MGD) is released?

question.prompt: In ≤140 words, explain why green infrastructure (rain gardens, bioswales, urban tree canopy) is now a central tool of contemporary urban-infrastructure design.
question.rubric: Mentions: Green infrastructure (GI) — rain gardens, bioswales, permeable pavement, green roofs, urban tree canopy, constructed wetlands — captures + filters + infiltrates stormwater *at the source* rather than at end-of-pipe. Frameworks: SUDS (UK), LID (US). Why central: (1) reduces combined-sewer-overflow volume + frequency in legacy CSS cities at lower capital cost than deep tunnels alone; (2) **co-benefits** — urban-heat-island reduction (lesson 7), biodiversity, urban-tree carbon, recreational + aesthetic + property value uplift, mental health, and equity if sited in underserved neighborhoods; (3) integrates with Complete Streets, 15-min city, Vision Zero (lesson 3) + with parking-minimum reform that reduces impervious coverage; (4) climate adaptation — more frequent extreme rainfall + heat events in a warming climate demand source-control resilience. Models: Philadelphia GCCW (\$2.4B), Portland Green Streets, NYC Bluebelts + Bioswales, Copenhagen Cloudburst, Singapore ABC Waters, Berlin Schwammstadt sponge-city.
